beats.text: One fight with your partner needs about five good moments to balance it.
A researcher filmed couples while they argued. Then checked who was still together years later.
Couples who lasted: about five good moments for every bad one. Even during the fight!
Couples close to a split: one to one, or less.
A joke. A touch. A nod. They add up. That's why

sources: Gottman & Levenson (1992), Marital processes predictive of later dissolution, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 63(2), 221–233; Gottman (1994), What Predicts Divorce? / Why Marriages Succeed or Fail – in stable couples about 5 positive interactions for every negative one during conflict; a ratio of about 1:1 or lower went with later separation (observational; the exact ratio is debated).
The Gottman Institute, 'The Magic Relationship Ratio, According to Science' – 5:1 during conflict; 1:1 or less 'teetering on the edge of divorce'.
